questions.q: What does an accounting calendar define for a ledger?
options: The period type, number of periods, their dates, and their names for a fiscal year
Which legal entities are assigned to the ledger
The currency conversion rate type
The ledger's chart of accounts segments
questions.explain: An accounting calendar breaks a fiscal year into accounting periods, defining period type, count, dates, and naming.

questions.q: What is a 13-period (or 4-4-5) calendar pattern typically used for?
options: Only for secondary ledgers, never primary ledgers
Companies, often retailers or manufacturers, that prefer equal-length accounting periods instead of irregular calendar months
It is required for every Oracle Fusion implementation
It replaces the need for a fiscal year
questions.explain: 13-period calendars use equal-length periods, often following a 4-4-5 week pattern, and are common among retailers and manufacturers.

questions.q: Does the fiscal year always have to start in January?
options: Fiscal years cannot be defined at all in Oracle Fusion
Yes, Oracle Fusion requires a January start
No — the accounting calendar definition includes the fiscal year's start month, which is not always January
Only secondary ledgers can start in a month other than January
questions.explain: Defining a calendar includes specifying the fiscal year's start month, which varies by company and is not required to be January.

questions.q: Why does consistent, clear period naming matter?
options: Period names are hidden from end users entirely
Period naming only matters for the chart of accounts
It has no practical effect on users
Users see period names on every transaction, report, and period-close screen for years, so confusing names cause reporting headaches
questions.explain: Period names appear everywhere transactions and reports reference time, so clarity and consistency genuinely matter long-term.

questions.q: Why is changing a calendar's structure after transactions have posted described as disruptive or nearly impossible?
options: Because Oracle Fusion automatically prevents any calendar from ever changing
Because splitting, renaming, or shifting periods that already have live transactions against them creates significant cleanup and reconciliation problems
Because calendars can only be changed by Oracle support directly
Because calendars have no connection to posted transactions
questions.explain: Once periods have live data posted against them, restructuring the calendar risks major disruption, which is why calendar design deserves careful upfront planning.
